title: Strength of Materials I
topics: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: A tie bar has a cross-sectional area of 200 mm2 and carries a load of 50 kN. What stress does it develop, in MPa?
items.s: Stress = load/area = 50000 N / 200 mm2 = 250 MPa.

items.q: What axial load, in kN, produces a stress of 150 MPa in a bar of area 600 mm2?
items.s: P = stress * area = 150 * 600 = 90000 N = 90 kN.

items.q: A material with a yield stress of 300 MPa is used at a working stress of 80 MPa. What is the factor of safety?
items.s: Factor of safety = failure stress/working stress = 300/80 = 3.75.

items.q: At a load of 0.02 kN a specimen of area 50 mm2 yields. What yield stress does this give, in MPa?
items.s: Yield stress = load/area = 20.0/50 = 0.4 MPa.

items.q: A cantilever of length 4 m carries a point load of 5 kN at its free end. What is the maximum bending moment, in kNm?
items.s: M = P*L = 5*4 = 20 kNm at the fixed end.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: A cantilever 3 m long carries 8 kN/m throughout. What is the shear force at the fixed end, in kN?
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: A rectangular beam section is 150 mm wide and 150 mm deep. Calculate its section modulus in mm3, in scientific form as a plain number.
A solid circular shaft of diameter 80 mm is used as a beam. What is its section modulus in mm3?
A rectangular beam is 150 mm deep. How far is the extreme fibre from the neutral axis, in mm?
items.s: Neutral axis is at mid-depth, so distance = h/2 = 150/2 = 75 mm.

items.q: A section of area 5000 mm2 carries a shear force of 20 kN. Calculate the average shear stress in MPa.
items.s: Average shear stress = V/A = 20000/5000 = 4 MPa.

items.q: For a solid circular section, what is the ratio of maximum shear stress to average shear stress? Give the value as a decimal to 2 places.
items.s: Max/average = 4/3 = 1.33 for a solid circle, against 1.5 for a rectangle.

items.q: A rectangular bar is 12 mm thick and 120 mm deep. What is its cross-sectional area in mm2?
items.s: Area = thickness x depth = 12 x 120 = 1440 mm2.

items.q: Calculate the polar moment of inertia of a solid circular section of diameter 50 mm, in mm4.
A beam of span 8000 mm is limited to span/500 deflection. What is the allowable deflection in mm?
items.s: Allowable deflection = L/500 = 8000/500 = 16 mm.

items.q: A bar 300 mm long extends by 2.4 mm under load. Determine the direct strain produced.
items.s: Strain = extension/original length = 2.4/300 = 0.008.

items.q: A steel rod of diameter 25 mm and length 2000 mm carries 50 kN. Taking E = 200 GPa, find the elongation in mm.
A material reaches a stress of 150 MPa at a strain of 0.001 while still elastic. Calculate its Young's modulus in GPa.
items.s: E = stress/strain = 150/0.001 = 150000.0 MPa = 150 GPa.

items.q: A specimen strained axially by 0.0006 shows a lateral strain of a magnitude given by Poisson's ratio 0.3. Determine the lateral strain.
items.s: Lateral strain = nu * longitudinal strain = 0.3*0.0006 = 0.00018.

items.q: A bar fully restrained at both ends is heated through 30 K. With coefficient of expansion 2.3e-05 /K and E = 210 GPa, find the thermal stress in MPa.
items.s: Free strain = a*dT = 2.3e-05*30 = 0.00069; stress = strain*E = 144.9 MPa.

items.q: A steel with ultimate strength 400 MPa is to be used with a factor of safety of 3. Find the allowable stress in MPa.
items.s: Allowable stress = failure stress/factor of safety = 400/3 = 133.3 MPa.

items.q: A tensile test piece of original gauge length 80 mm breaks at a gauge length of 104.0 mm. Calculate the percentage elongation.
A specimen of original area 250 mm2 necks to 125.0 mm2 at fracture. Determine the percentage reduction in area.
A material with no distinct yield point is specified by a proof stress of 350 MPa at 0.1% strain. What strain corresponds to that proof stress?
A bar of gauge length 80 mm extends to 104.0 mm before breaking. What average strain did it sustain?
For E = 210 GPa and Poisson's ratio 0.28, calculate the bulk modulus in GPa.
A cantilever 1 m long carries a uniformly distributed load of 4 kN/m over its whole length. Find the maximum bending moment in kNm.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a central point load of 6 kN. What is the maximum bending moment in kNm?
items.s: R = P/2 per support; M = P*L/4 = 6*6/4 = 9 kNm.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a uniform load of 8 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kNm.
items.s: M = wL^2/8 = 8*10^2/8 = 100 kNm at midspan.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a central point load of 6 kN. What is the shear force just to the left of midspan, in kN?
items.s: Each reaction = P/2 = 6/2 = 3 kN, so the shear just left of midspan is 3 kN.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a single concentrated load at 2.5 m from the left support. At what distance from the left support is the shear force zero, in m?
items.s: Shear changes sign directly under the load, so the zero-shear section is at 2.5 m from the left support.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 8 m carries a uniform load of 4 kN/m. At what distance from a support does the bending moment become zero again beyond midspan, in m?
items.s: The moment is zero only at the supports, so from the left support it is zero at 0 and 8 m; beyond midspan the next zero is at 4 m.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: A beam of rectangular section 75 mm by 250 mm carries a bending moment of 8 kNm. Find the maximum bending stress in MPa.
A bending moment of 25 kNm must be carried with a maximum stress of 100 MPa. What section modulus is required, in mm3?
A beam with EI = 205 GPa x 80 x 10^6 mm4 carries a moment of 10 kNm. Find the radius of curvature in mm.
A hollow circular beam has outer diameter 150 mm and wall thickness 10 mm. Calculate its section modulus in mm3.
A simply supported beam of section modulus 1400000 mm3 carries 25 kN/m and is limited to 120 MPa. Find the maximum span in m.
A rectangular section 100 mm wide and 200 mm deep carries a shear force of 80 kN. Find the maximum shear stress in MPa.
items.s: tau_max = 1.5V/A = 1.5*80000/20000 = 6 MPa at the neutral axis.

items.q: A solid circular section of diameter 150 mm carries a shear force of 90 kN. What is the maximum shear stress in MPa?
For a rectangular section 60 mm by 300 mm carrying 100 kN, find the shear stress at 75.0 mm from the neutral axis, in MPa.
items.s: tau = taumax[1-(2y/h)^2], taumax = 8.33 MPa, so tau = 6.25 MPa.

items.q: A rectangular beam 100 mm wide and 250 mm deep is limited to a maximum shear stress of 2 MPa. What shear force can it carry, in kN?
A beam carries 60 kN. With Q = 400 x 10^3 mm3 and I = 40 x 10^6 mm4, find the shear flow in N/mm.
A solid steel shaft of diameter 100 mm transmits a torque of 3 kNm. Find the maximum shear stress in MPa.
What diameter, in mm, is needed for a solid shaft to transmit 4 kNm with a maximum shear stress of 50 MPa?
A shaft of diameter 80 mm and length 3000 mm carries 4 kNm. With G = 82 GPa, find the angle of twist in radians.
A shaft transmits 45 kW at 1000 rev/min. What torque does it carry, in Nm?
A hollow shaft has outer diameter 80 mm and inner diameter 64 mm. Find its polar moment of inertia in mm4.
For a shaft of diameter 60 mm in a material of G = 82 GPa, calculate the torsional rigidity GJ in Nmm2.
A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a central load of 10 kN. With EI = 200 GPa x 60 x 10^6 mm4, find the central deflection in mm.
A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries 10 kN/m. Taking EI = 210 GPa x 100 x 10^6 mm4, find the midspan deflection in mm.

A propped cantilever of span 2 m carries a uniform load of 5 kN/m. What is the prop reaction, in kN?
At a point the direct stresses are 40 MPa and 30 MPa with a shear stress of 30 MPa. Find the major principal stress in MPa.
For direct stresses 140 MPa and 20 MPa with shear 30 MPa, what is the maximum shear stress at the point, in MPa?
With direct stresses 100 MPa and 30 MPa and shear stress 35 MPa, find the minor principal stress in MPa.

items.q: The Mohr circle for the stress state 100 MPa, 20 MPa and shear 50 MPa has what radius in MPa?
Find the angle of the principal plane, in degrees, for 120 MPa, 40 MPa and shear 30 MPa.
items.s: tan(2theta) = 2*tau/(sx - sy), so 2theta = 36.87 degrees and theta = 18.43 degrees.

items.q: A column of area 10000 mm2 and section modulus 400000 mm3 carries 100 kN at an eccentricity of 20 mm. Find the maximum stress in MPa.
items.s: Direct = 10.0 MPa; bending = 5.0 MPa; maximum = 15 MPa.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Equivalent stress.
o: a single stress used to compare a complex stress state with the strength from a simple test
the line across a beam section where bending stress is zero
the state of stress in which stresses act in one plane only
a technique of writing one bending moment equation for the whole beam using step brackets
items.s: Equivalent stress: a single stress used to compare a complex stress state with the strength from a simple test. The other options describe Macaulay's method, Two dimensional stress system, Neutral axis.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ability of a material to absorb energy before fracture”?
o: Ultimate tensile strength
Factor of safety
Toughness
Percentage elongation
items.s: Toughness is the ability of a material to absorb energy before fracture.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Direct stress.
o: the intensity of force per unit area acting along the plane of a section, varying across the depth
the internal intensity of force per unit area acting normal to a section, measured in N/mm2 or MPa
the ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain, with a typical value of about 0.3 for steel
the ratio of the second moment of area to the distance from the neutral axis, a measure of bending strength
items.s: Direct stress: the internal intensity of force per unit area acting normal to a section, measured in N/mm2 or MPa. The other options describe Shear stress in a beam, Section modulus, Poisson's ratio.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Proof stress?
o: a hollow shaft carries more torque for the same mass because material is placed far from the axis
the displacement of a point on a beam from its unloaded position
the stress that produces a specified small permanent strain in a material with no distinct yield point
the radius of the circular arc into which a bent beam deflects
items.s: Proof stress: the stress that produces a specified small permanent strain in a material with no distinct yield point. The other options describe Radius of curvature, Hollow shaft advantage, Deflection.

items.q: Which term is described by “the change in length of a member divided by its original length, a dimensionless ratio”?
o: Poisson's ratio
Direct stress
Direct strain
Hooke's law
items.s: Direct strain is the change in length of a member divided by its original length, a dimensionless ratio.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ratio of direct stress to direct strain within the elastic limit of a material”?
o: Direct strain
Thermal stress
Young's modulus
Direct stress
items.s: Young's modulus is the ratio of direct stress to direct strain within the elastic limit of a material.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Brittleness?
o: the angle between the tangent to the deflected beam and its original axis
the outermost fibre of a beam section where bending stress is greatest
the increase in gauge length at fracture expressed as a percentage of the original gauge length
the tendency of a material to fracture with little or no plastic deformation
items.s: Brittleness: the tendency of a material to fracture with little or no plastic deformation. The other options describe Percentage elongation, Slope, Extreme fibre.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Slope?
o: a load spread at a constant intensity along the length of a beam
a single stress used to compare a complex stress state with the strength from a simple test
the direct stress set up across a section of a beam by the bending moment
the angle between the tangent to the deflected beam and its original axis
items.s: Slope: the angle between the tangent to the deflected beam and its original axis. The other options describe Equivalent stress, Uniformly distributed load, Bending stress.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Eccentric loading?
o: the load per unit deflection of a beam at the point where the load acts
the ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain, with a typical value of about 0.3 for steel
the application of a load away from the centroid of a section, producing direct stress and bending
the stresses added algebraically when a member carries axial load and bending together
items.s: Eccentric loading: the application of a load away from the centroid of a section, producing direct stress and bending. The other options describe Poisson's ratio, Direct and bending stress, Stiffness of a beam.

items.q: Simply supported beam may be defined as
o: a beam resting freely on supports at both ends
the relation that shear stress over radius equals twisting moment over polar moment of inertia
the stress at which a material begins to deform permanently
a beam fixed at one end and free at the other
items.s: Simply supported beam: a beam resting freely on supports at both ends. The other options describe Yield stress, Torsion equation, Cantilever.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: The statement “the load per unit deflection of a beam at the point where the load acts” describes which of the following?
o: Propped cantilever
Stiffness of a beam
Deflection
Double integration method
items.s: Stiffness of a beam is the load per unit deflection of a beam at the point where the load acts.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Second moment of area.
o: the highest shear stress on a section, occurring at the neutral axis for a rectangular section
the line across a beam section where bending stress is zero
the shear stress that must act on perpendicular planes to keep a small element in equilibrium
the geometrical property of a section that measures how its area is distributed about an axis
items.s: Second moment of area: the geometrical property of a section that measures how its area is distributed about an axis. The other options describe Maximum shear stress, Complimentary shear, Neutral axis.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Slope.
o: the tendency of a material to fracture with little or no plastic deformation
the angle between the tangent to the deflected beam and its original axis
a hollow shaft carries more torque for the same mass because material is placed far from the axis
the displacement of a point on a beam from its unloaded position
items.s: Slope: the angle between the tangent to the deflected beam and its original axis. The other options describe Hollow shaft advantage, Deflection, Brittleness.

items.q: Complimentary shear may be defined as
o: the shear stress that must act on perpendicular planes to keep a small element in equilibrium
the radius of the circular arc into which a bent beam deflects
the increase in gauge length at fracture expressed as a percentage of the original gauge length
a single stress used to compare a complex stress state with the strength from a simple test
items.s: Complimentary shear: the shear stress that must act on perpendicular planes to keep a small element in equilibrium. The other options describe Radius of curvature, Percentage elongation, Equivalent stress.

items.q: Which term is described by “a beam resting freely on supports at both ends”?
o: Point of contraflexure
Simply supported beam
Shear force
Bending moment
items.s: Simply supported beam is a beam resting freely on supports at both ends.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: Ultimate tensile strength may be defined as
o: the greatest stress a material attains before it breaks in tension
a cantilever given an additional support at its free end
the internal intensity of force per unit area acting normal to a section, measured in N/mm2 or MPa
the line across a beam section where bending stress is zero
items.s: Ultimate tensile strength: the greatest stress a material attains before it breaks in tension. The other options describe Propped cantilever, Neutral axis, Direct stress.

items.q: Hollow shaft advantage may be defined as
o: a beam resting freely on supports at both ends
a hollow shaft carries more torque for the same mass because material is placed far from the axis
the state of stress in which stresses act in one plane only
the shear stress that must act on perpendicular planes to keep a small element in equilibrium
items.s: Hollow shaft advantage: a hollow shaft carries more torque for the same mass because material is placed far from the axis. The other options describe Complimentary shear, Simply supported beam, Two dimensional stress system.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Maximum shear stress?
o: the theory that plane sections remain plane and stress varies linearly from the neutral axis
a beam resting freely on supports at both ends
the highest shear stress on a section, occurring at the neutral axis for a rectangular section
the ratio of the failure stress to the working or allowable stress
items.s: Maximum shear stress: the highest shear stress on a section, occurring at the neutral axis for a rectangular section. The other options describe Simply supported beam, Simple bending theory, Factor of safety.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Principal stress.
o: the normal stress on a plane where the shear stress is zero
the application of a load away from the centroid of a section, producing direct stress and bending
the state of stress in which stresses act in one plane only
the stresses added algebraically when a member carries axial load and bending together
items.s: Principal stress: the normal stress on a plane where the shear stress is zero. The other options describe Direct and bending stress, Two dimensional stress system, Eccentric loading.

items.q: Brittleness may be defined as
o: the plane on which the shear stress is zero and the normal stress is greatest or least
a load spread at a constant intensity along the length of a beam
the geometrical property of a section that measures how its area is distributed about an axis
the tendency of a material to fracture with little or no plastic deformation
items.s: Brittleness: the tendency of a material to fracture with little or no plastic deformation. The other options describe Uniformly distributed load, Second moment of area, Principal plane.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Toughness?
o: the ability of a material to absorb energy before fracture
the relation that shear stress over radius equals twisting moment over polar moment of inertia
the twisting moment applied to a shaft about its longitudinal axis
a cantilever given an additional support at its free end
items.s: Toughness: the ability of a material to absorb energy before fracture. The other options describe Torsion equation, Propped cantilever, Torsion.

items.q: Second moment of area may be defined as
o: the algebraic sum of the vertical forces acting to one side of a section of a beam
the geometrical property of a section that measures how its area is distributed about an axis
the relation that shear stress over radius equals twisting moment over polar moment of inertia
the shear stress that must act on perpendicular planes to keep a small element in equilibrium
items.s: Second moment of area: the geometrical property of a section that measures how its area is distributed about an axis. The other options describe Complimentary shear, Shear force, Torsion equation.

items.q: The statement “a single stress used to compare a complex stress state with the strength from a simple test” describes which of the following?
o: Mohr's circle
Equivalent stress
Principal stress
Direct and bending stress
items.s: Equivalent stress is a single stress used to compare a complex stress state with the strength from a simple test.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Maximum shear stress?
o: the load per unit deflection of a beam at the point where the load acts
a cantilever given an additional support at its free end
the algebraic sum of the vertical forces acting to one side of a section of a beam
the highest shear stress on a section, occurring at the neutral axis for a rectangular section
items.s: Maximum shear stress: the highest shear stress on a section, occurring at the neutral axis for a rectangular section. The other options describe Stiffness of a beam, Propped cantilever, Shear force.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Shear force.
o: the algebraic sum of the vertical forces acting to one side of a section of a beam
the ratio of direct stress to volumetric strain for a material under uniform pressure
the strain measured across the axis of a loaded member
the displacement of a point on a beam from its unloaded position
items.s: Shear force: the algebraic sum of the vertical forces acting to one side of a section of a beam. The other options describe Deflection, Bulk modulus, Lateral strain.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: Which term is described by “the algebraic sum of the moments of the forces about a section of a beam”?
o: Shear force
Bending moment
Simply supported beam
Uniformly distributed load
items.s: Bending moment is the algebraic sum of the moments of the forces about a section of a beam.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: The statement “the shear force per unit length along the length of a member” describes which of the following?
o: Shear diagram for a rectangle
Shear flow
Average shear stress
Complimentary shear
items.s: Shear flow is the shear force per unit length along the length of a member.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Polar moment of inertia?
o: the application of a load away from the centroid of a section, producing direct stress and bending
the ratio of direct stress to direct strain within the elastic limit of a material
the second moment of area of a circular section about its polar axis
the method of obtaining slope and deflection by integrating the bending moment equation twice
items.s: Polar moment of inertia: the second moment of area of a circular section about its polar axis. The other options describe Double integration method, Young's modulus, Eccentric loading.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ratio of the second moment of area to the distance from the neutral axis, a measure of bending strength”?
o: Neutral axis
Section modulus
Radius of curvature
Simple bending theory
items.s: Section modulus is the ratio of the second moment of area to the distance from the neutral axis, a measure of bending strength.

items.q: Toughness may be defined as
o: the tendency of a material to fracture with little or no plastic deformation
the theory that plane sections remain plane and stress varies linearly from the neutral axis
the ability of a material to absorb energy before fracture
the method of obtaining slope and deflection by integrating the bending moment equation twice
items.s: Toughness: the ability of a material to absorb energy before fracture. The other options describe Brittleness, Double integration method, Simple bending theory.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Simple bending theory?
o: the ratio of the failure stress to the working or allowable stress
the highest shear stress on a section, occurring at the neutral axis for a rectangular section
the plane on which the shear stress is zero and the normal stress is greatest or least
the theory that plane sections remain plane and stress varies linearly from the neutral axis
items.s: Simple bending theory: the theory that plane sections remain plane and stress varies linearly from the neutral axis. The other options describe Principal plane, Factor of safety, Maximum shear stress.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Mohr's circle?
o: the internal intensity of force per unit area acting normal to a section, measured in N/mm2 or MPa
the second moment of area of a circular section about its polar axis
a graphical construction used to find principal stresses and maximum shear stress at a point
the ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain, with a typical value of about 0.3 for steel
items.s: Mohr's circle: a graphical construction used to find principal stresses and maximum shear stress at a point. The other options describe Direct stress, Poisson's ratio, Polar moment of inertia.

items.q: Which term is described by “the tendency of a material to fracture with little or no plastic deformation”?
o: Percentage elongation
Factor of safety
Ductility
Brittleness
items.s: Brittleness is the tendency of a material to fracture with little or no plastic deformation.

items.q: Shear diagram for a rectangle may be defined as
o: the intensity of force per unit area acting along the plane of a section, varying across the depth
a beam resting freely on supports at both ends
the parabolic variation of shear stress across the depth of a rectangular section
the plane on which the shear stress is zero and the normal stress is greatest or least
items.s: Shear diagram for a rectangle: the parabolic variation of shear stress across the depth of a rectangular section. The other options describe Shear stress in a beam, Principal plane, Simply supported beam.

items.q: Mohr's circle may be defined as
o: a graphical construction used to find principal stresses and maximum shear stress at a point
the statement that stress is proportional to strain up to the elastic limit
the load per unit deflection of a beam at the point where the load acts
the plane on which the shear stress is zero and the normal stress is greatest or least
items.s: Mohr's circle: a graphical construction used to find principal stresses and maximum shear stress at a point. The other options describe Stiffness of a beam, Hooke's law, Principal plane.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Torsional rigidity.
o: the algebraic sum of the moments of the forces about a section of a beam
the parabolic variation of shear stress across the depth of a rectangular section
the product of the shear modulus and the polar moment of inertia, which resists twisting
the theory that plane sections remain plane and stress varies linearly from the neutral axis
items.s: Torsional rigidity: the product of the shear modulus and the polar moment of inertia, which resists twisting. The other options describe Shear diagram for a rectangle, Bending moment, Simple bending theory.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Neutral axis?
o: the direct stress set up across a section of a beam by the bending moment
the line across a beam section where bending stress is zero
the ratio of direct stress to direct strain within the elastic limit of a material
the application of a load away from the centroid of a section, producing direct stress and bending
items.s: Neutral axis: the line across a beam section where bending stress is zero. The other options describe Young's modulus, Eccentric loading, Bending stress.

items.q: All of the following belong to Simple stress and strain EXCEPT
o: Direct strain
Direct stress
Torsion equation
Young's modulus
items.s: Every other option belongs to Simple stress and strain. “Torsion equation” belongs to Torsion of circular shafts, not Simple stress and strain.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Radius of curvature?
o: a beam fixed at one end and free at the other
the radius of the circular arc into which a bent beam deflects
the line across a beam section where bending stress is zero
the greatest stress a material attains before it breaks in tension
items.s: Radius of curvature: the radius of the circular arc into which a bent beam deflects. The other options describe Neutral axis, Cantilever, Ultimate tensile strength.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Proof stress?
o: a technique of writing one bending moment equation for the whole beam using step brackets
the application of a load away from the centroid of a section, producing direct stress and bending
the stress that produces a specified small permanent strain in a material with no distinct yield point
the method of obtaining slope and deflection by integrating the bending moment equation twice
items.s: Proof stress: the stress that produces a specified small permanent strain in a material with no distinct yield point. The other options describe Macaulay's method, Eccentric loading, Double integration method.

items.q: Which term is described by “the angle through which one end of a shaft rotates relative to the other under torsion”?
o: Torsion equation
Hollow shaft advantage
Angle of twist
Bulk modulus
items.s: Angle of twist is the angle through which one end of a shaft rotates relative to the other under torsion.

items.q: Bending stress may be defined as
o: the direct stress set up across a section of a beam by the bending moment
a point in a beam where the bending moment changes sign
the stresses added algebraically when a member carries axial load and bending together
the section of a beam where the shear force is zero, where the bending moment is greatest
items.s: Bending stress: the direct stress set up across a section of a beam by the bending moment. The other options describe Direct and bending stress, Point of contraflexure, Point of zero shear.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Shear stress in a beam?
o: the statement that stress is proportional to strain up to the elastic limit
the parabolic variation of shear stress across the depth of a rectangular section
a point in a beam where the bending moment changes sign
the intensity of force per unit area acting along the plane of a section, varying across the depth
items.s: Shear stress in a beam: the intensity of force per unit area acting along the plane of a section, varying across the depth. The other options describe Hooke's law, Shear diagram for a rectangle, Point of contraflexure.

items.q: All of the following belong to Mechanical properties of materials EXCEPT
o: Factor of safety
Ultimate tensile strength
Yield stress
Flexural rigidity
items.s: Every other option belongs to Mechanical properties of materials. “Flexural rigidity” belongs to Deflection of beams, not Mechanical properties of materials.

items.q: The statement “a hollow shaft carries more torque for the same mass because material is placed far from the axis” describes which of the following?
o: Bulk modulus
Hollow shaft advantage
Torsion
Polar moment of inertia
items.s: Hollow shaft advantage is a hollow shaft carries more torque for the same mass because material is placed far from the axis.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Bending moment.
o: the change in length of a member divided by its original length, a dimensionless ratio
the method of obtaining slope and deflection by integrating the bending moment equation twice
the algebraic sum of the vertical forces acting to one side of a section of a beam
the algebraic sum of the moments of the forces about a section of a beam
items.s: Bending moment: the algebraic sum of the moments of the forces about a section of a beam. The other options describe Double integration method, Direct strain, Shear force.
items.t: Shear force and bending moment diagrams

items.q: Torsion may be defined as
o: the greatest stress a material can carry and still return to its original length when unloaded
the angle between the tangent to the deflected beam and its original axis

items.q: Three of these relate to Combined stresses. Which one does not?
o: Principal stress
Bulk modulus
Maximum shear stress
Principal plane
items.s: Every other option belongs to Combined stresses. “Bulk modulus” belongs to Torsion of circular shafts, not Combined stresses.
